summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for $geoNear Aggregation Stage; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: 6. Views do not support `$geoNear`. Reads on a view are executed as part of the view's underlying aggregation pipeline, so the stage can never occupy first position. The MongoDB 3.4 manual states this as an explicit restriction ("Views do not support geoNear operations"). — https://docs.huihoo.com/mongodb/3.4/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/index.html
**Concept:** `$geoNear` Aggregation Stage **Parent domain:** MongoDB Geospatial **Date:** 2026-09-18 **Report type:** mechanism / internal structure

**D3 — `$geoNear` on views.** A search-surfaced snippet attributed to MongoDB documentation states *"Views do not support geoNear operations (i.e. geoNear command and $geoNear pipeline stage)."* I fetched https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views/ directly and that page does not contain the statement; it defers to a "Supported Operations" sub-page I did not retrieve. The claim is plausible and consistent with A2 (a view's own pipeline occupies the first position), but it is **snippet-sourced, not primary-verified**.

7. `includeLocs` writes back which location value was used for the calculation. This matters only when a document holds several candidate locations (an array of points), where the emitted distance is otherwise unattributable. <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/>

3. `$geoNear` requires a geospatial index (`2d` or `2dsphere`). In 2.4 the stage additionally required that the collection have *at most* one `2d` index and/or one `2dsphere` index, because there was no way to disambiguate. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v2.4/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt

8. When `key` is omitted and a single geospatial index exists, MongoDB looks first for a `2d` index and only then for a `2dsphere` index. This is a silent semantics hazard: adding a legacy `2d` index to a collection that already has a `2dsphere` index changes which geometry and which distance units an existing `$geoNear` query uses, with no query-level change. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/

19. `distanceMultiplier` is the documented mechanism for unit correction — "use the `distanceMultiplier` to convert radians, as returned by a spherical query, to kilometers by multiplying by the radius of the Earth". It is applied to the output distance, so it does **not** rescale `minDistance`/`maxDistance`; those remain in the native unit. Mixing the two is a distinct trap. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/master/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt

30. `includeLocs` exists specifically because a single document can hold multiple locations: it names an output field "that identifies the location used to calculate the distance". Without it, a multi-location document's distance is unattributable to a specific point. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/master/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt

1. **Are distance units index-driven or coordinate-format-driven?** Primary MongoDB sources are unambiguous that they are format-driven: meters for a GeoJSON `near`, radians for a legacy pair (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/master/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt, corroborated by https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nearSphere/). A substantial body of third-party writing instead states the rule as index-driven — "2dsphere returns meters, 2d returns radians" — which happens to give the right answer only because GeoJSON is normally paired

24. Practical consequence of claims 22 and 23: `$geoNear` is the right stage when distance ordering is the primary access path, and the wrong stage when distance is a secondary filter under a more selective predicate or a different sort key. In the latter case a non-sorting containment predicate inside an ordinary `$match` leaves the planner free to choose the selective index. <https://thecodebarbarian.com/80-20-guide-to-mongodb-geospatial-queries>

That's ~4 fetches and would close G1–G3 and G9. 3. The `$geoNear` frontier item stays unmerged into `tree.json` per your instruction — confirm that's still right, or say when you want it promoted.

5. **Whether `$geoNear` can exploit a non-geo prefix of a compound 2dsphere index to pre-filter.** Several third-party posts recommend a compound index such as `{category: 1, location: "2dsphere"}` so that the `query` option filters before the proximity scan, and claim large speedups. The `$geoNear` reference page does not document this, and the `key` option is defined in terms of the indexed geospatial field path only. I found no primary confirmation and no `explain` output demonstrating prefix bounds being generated for a `$geoNear` `query` predicate. **Treat the compound-index recommendatio

**C3. Child stages may return the same document more than once, so `NearStage` deduplicates by record id using a `RecordIdDeduplicator`, tracking membership in `_seenDocuments` and removing an entry when the document is emitted.** Duplicate emission is a structural hazard of covering a region with overlapping index cells; deduplication is where it is handled.

**D9. Where a document holds both a legacy coordinate pair and a GeoJSON representation, which one gets indexed changed at MongoDB 8.2:** before 8.2 the index stored the first supported representation (legacy pair, if the first two fields are numeric); from 8.2 it always indexes the GeoJSON representation when one is present. This can shift `$geoNear` distances across an upgrade for such documents.

14. Because `$geoNear` binds to a geospatial index and 2dsphere indexes are always sparse, documents lacking the indexed field — or holding `null` or an empty array there — are not indexed and therefore never returned by `$geoNear`. MongoDB ignores the `sparse` option on 2dsphere index creation. <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/2dsphere/>

39. `$geoNear` executes as an expanding sequence of distance intervals, and this is visible in `explain`. A reported case on ~1M documents with `maxDistance: 7738757` (≈7,700 km) shows four intervals returning 254 / 929,329 / 93,204 / 15,866 results, examining 1,038,862 documents and taking 12,643 ms. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/geonear-performance/247179

**Seven gaps closed by cross-reference.** The strongest: mechanism.md flagged the "16 MB limit on `$geoNear`" as unverifiable and guessed it was a carry-over from the legacy command — edge-cases.md has the primary Jira ticket (`SERVER-18965`, fix version 4.2) confirming it was real pre-4.2 *and* that it **silently discarded documents**, and history.md supplies the mechanism of the fix (`SERVER-22949` moved the command into the aggregation framework). Also: history.md, edge-cases.md and practice.md each independently declared sharded merge behaviour undocumented — all three searched the sharded
**Concept:** `$geoNear` aggregation stage (MongoDB) **Parent domain:** MongoDB Geospatial **Report date:** 2026-09-18 **Report type:** boundary conditions / failure modes / disagreements

This report covers only the `$geoNear` aggregation pipeline stage: its positional and index preconditions, its unit semantics, its version-dependent option surface, its documented and reported error conditions, and its performance boundary. It deliberately excludes `$near`, `$nearSphere`, `$geoWithin`, `$geoIntersects`, 2d/2dsphere index internals, and geospatial modelling in general, except where a fact about one of those is a direct precondition of `$geoNear` behaviour. Those are separate frontier items.

1. `$geoNear` can only be used as the first stage of a pipeline. The server error text is `$geoNear is only valid as the first stage in a pipeline`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/ · https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/issues/8928

2. The "first stage" rule is scoped to a pipeline, not to the whole aggregation. `$geoNear` is legal as the first stage of a `$lookup` sub-pipeline. Before the fix it failed with error code `50860`; `SERVER-38716` ("fix `$geoNear` and `$text` within `$lookup` sub-pipeline") is Closed/Fixed with fix version **4.1.8**, and reproduced on 3.6.9, 4.0.5 and 4.1.7. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-38716

29. You cannot place a `$near` or `$nearSphere` predicate in the `query` option of `$geoNear`, and the `near` argument cannot appear inside `query`. There is no supported way to express two proximity constraints in one `$geoNear` stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/ · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/master/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt

4. MongoDB 2.4 shipped the stage with `near`, `distanceField`, `query`, `maxDistance`, `spherical`, `limit`, `num`, `distanceMultiplier`, `includeLocs`, and `uniqueDocs`. `limit` defaulted to 100 documents, and `num` overrode `limit` when both were given. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v2.4/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt

8. In MongoDB 4.0 the stage still documented `limit` (default 100), `num`, and `uniqueDocs`. All three are absent from the 4.2 branch source. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v4.0/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v4.2/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt

10. The `geoNear` command was removed in MongoDB 4.2: "Starting in version 4.2, MongoDB removes the `geoNear` command. Use the `$geoNear` aggregation stage instead." The 4.2 compatibility notes carry a dedicated section titled "Remove `limit` and `num` Options from `$geoNear`". — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v4.2/source/release-notes/4.2-compatibility.txt

11. MongoDB 4.2 removed the `limit` and `num` options from `$geoNear` and removed the implicit default limit of 100: "Starting in version 4.2, `$geoNear` no longer has a default limit of 100 documents." Callers must now append an explicit `$limit` stage. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v4.2/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v4.2/source/release-notes/4.2-compatibility.txt

12. The engineering cause is SERVER-22949, "Remove default limit from $geoNear", fixed in 4.1.1 (the development series that became 4.2) and resolved 2018-06-19. The work moved the `geoNear` command into the aggregation framework; the resolution states the rewrite "removes the limit in the `$geoNear` aggregation stage. To limit the number of results, use a `$limit` stage." It was filed to match SERVER-14515, which had earlier removed the default limit from `$near`/`$nearSphere`. So the stage's 4.2 form is a reimplementation, not a parameter tweak. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-22949

**B5. The `query` option cannot contain a `$near` predicate.** More generally a pipeline cannot carry both a `$geoNear` stage and a separate `near`-family predicate; the server rejects it with `BadValue Too many geoNear expressions`. The single-sort-source constraint is what this error protects. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/ · https://groups.google.com/g/mongodb-user/c/rdMrdwWko54

**D2 — the "16 MB BSON limit on `$geoNear`" claim.** A widely repeated claim holds that `$geoNear` results are capped by the 16 MB BSON document limit. This is very likely a carry-over from the legacy `geoNear` *database command*, which returned a single document containing an array of results and was therefore genuinely bound by 16 MB. The aggregation stage returns a cursor, so the same bound should not apply. **I could not verify this either way from a primary source** — the MongoDB v4.0 `geoNear` command reference page did not resolve on fetch, and the claim appears only in mailing-list pro

9. Because of rule 8, `$geoNear` cannot be used inside `$facet`; it appears on the `$facet` list of disallowed stages alongside `$out`, `$merge`, `$indexStats`, `$planCacheStats`, `$search`, `$searchMeta`, and `$vectorSearch`. <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet/>

12. You cannot put a `$near` predicate inside the `query` field of `$geoNear`. Documented wording: "You cannot specify a `$near` predicate in the `query` field of the `$geoNear` stage." <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/>

17. The standalone `geoNear` database command was deprecated and its `limit`/`num` options — and the implicit 100-document default limit — were removed in MongoDB 4.2; the aggregation stage is the supported replacement. Current documentation states plainly: "`$geoNear` no longer has a default limit of 100 documents." <https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/compatibility-changes-in-mongodb-4-2> <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/>

29. Portability consequence of claims 27 and 28: a `$geoNear` stage is not safely portable across MongoDB-compatible engines. A pipeline that omits `key` works on MongoDB with one geo index and fails on Cosmos DB vCore; a pipeline that sets `limit` works on DocumentDB and is invalid on MongoDB 4.2+; and a missing index degrades silently to a scan on Cosmos DB where MongoDB would have errored loudly. <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/vcore/geospatial-support> <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/geoNear.html> <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual

7. `$geoNear` requires a geospatial index (`2d` or `2dsphere`). It cannot fall back to a collection scan the way a non-geo sort can. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/

21. Through MongoDB 4.0, `$geoNear` accepted `limit` with a **default of 100 documents**, plus a functionally equivalent `num` option that overrode `limit` when both were given. A pipeline with no explicit limit silently returned at most 100 documents. — https://docs.huihoo.com/mongodb/3.4/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/index.html

22. MongoDB 4.2 removed the `limit` and `num` options **and** the default limit of 100. Result-count restriction must now be expressed as a separate `$limit` stage. The `geoNear` database command was removed in the same release. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/rapid/release-notes/4.2-compatibility/

26. `distanceField` was required for all collections through MongoDB 8.0. Starting in **8.1** it is optional for non-timeseries collections, and it remains required for timeseries collections. A pipeline that omits it is a syntax error on ≤8.0 and valid on ≥8.1. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/master/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/

35. MongoDB **8.0** tightened validation: `$near`, `$nearSphere` and `$geoNear` validate that a specified GeoJSON point has type `Point`, and any other type returns an error. This is a breaking change for pipelines that previously passed a `LineString`, `Polygon` or malformed object and got results anyway. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/

8. **The 8.0 compatibility page and the `$geoNear` reference page do not agree on specificity.** The reference page names `$near`, `$nearSphere` and `$geoNear` and the `Point`-type requirement; the release notes say only "malformed input" without naming operators or defining malformed. Anyone planning an 8.0 upgrade cannot enumerate the breaking surface from the release notes alone. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/ · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/release-notes/8.0-compatibility/

Archival mirror used for historical behaviour no longer in the current manual: - https://docs.huihoo.com/mongodb/3.4/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/index.html — MongoDB 3.4 manual: `limit` default 100, `num` override, one-index-per-type rule, views unsupported

5. `uniqueDocs` was deprecated as of MongoDB 2.6, because geospatial queries stopped returning duplicate results. — https://docs.huihoo.com/mongodb/3.4/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/index.html

16. MongoDB 5.3: `$geoNear` became usable on any field in a time series collection. On time series collections `key` must be specified and the `query` field cannot be used. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v8.0/source/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.txt — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/

19. MongoDB 8.0 tightened input validation: "Starting in MongoDB 8.0, `$near`, `$nearSphere`, and `$geoNear` validate that the type of the specified GeoJSON points is `Point`. Any other input type returns an error." Previously a non-`Point` GeoJSON type could be passed without an explicit error. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/ — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/operator/aggregation/geonear/

21. The current option set is `near` (required), `distanceField`, `distanceMultiplier`, `includeLocs`, `key`, `maxDistance`, `minDistance`, `query`, and `spherical` (default `false`). `limit`, `num`, and `uniqueDocs` are gone. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/

22. Current index-selection rule: if more than one `2d` index or more than one `2dsphere` index exists and `key` is not given, MongoDB returns an error. If at most one of each exists and `key` is omitted, MongoDB looks for a `2d` index first and falls back to a `2dsphere` index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/

2. **API-compatible products diverge on the removed options (disconfirming source).** Amazon DocumentDB's `$geoNear` reference documents a `limit` parameter as a supported option of the stage. That contradicts MongoDB 4.2+ behavior, where `limit` was removed and produces an error. This is a real divergence between DocumentDB's MongoDB-compatible API and MongoDB itself, not an error in the MongoDB record — but it means "the `$geoNear` stage" does not name one fixed contract once non-MongoDB implementations are in play. — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/geoNear.html

**D5. From MongoDB 8.0, `$near`, `$nearSphere`, and `$geoNear` validate that a supplied GeoJSON object has `type: "Point"`; any other GeoJSON type is rejected with an error.** Before 8.0 this was not enforced at the stage.
**E1. `$geoNear` has no default result limit in current MongoDB.** To bound the result set, follow the stage with a `$limit` stage.

**E2. This is a behaviour change, not an original design: MongoDB 4.2 removed the `limit` and `num` options from `$geoNear` along with the previous default limit of 100 documents.** Code written against 4.0 or earlier that relied on the implicit cap returns the full matching set after upgrade. Sources: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/compatibility-changes-in-mongodb-4-2 · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.2/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/

**E3. An independent reimplementation disagrees on the current surface: Amazon DocumentDB's `$geoNear` documentation still lists `limit` as a supported optional parameter.** Treat `$geoNear` option support as engine-specific, not as a property of the stage in the abstract.

10. Views do not support `geoNear` operations, so a proximity query cannot be pushed onto a pre-filtered view. This closes the most obvious workaround for the selectivity problem in claim 18. <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet/> (corroborated as the accepted answer in the 2022 MongoDB community thread: <https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/slow-performance-when-using-aggregation-along-with-geonear-with-multiple-query-condition/167850>)

16. On timeseries collections the contract is narrower: `key` must be specified, and the `query` field cannot be used at all. Documented wording: "you cannot use the `query` field for `$geoNear` on a time series collection. You must specify the `key` field for `$geoNear` on a time series collection." <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/> Timeseries collections support `$geoNear` only against 2dsphere indexes. <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations/>

27. Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore) diverges from MongoDB on both sides of the index contract. `key` is *always* required — omitting it raises `Error: $geoNear requires a 'key' option as a String` — while the geospatial index itself is *not* required: `$geoNear`, `$near`, and `$nearSphere` "don't have strict index requirements, so these queries wouldn't fail if an index is missing." Indexes are recommended, not enforced. <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/vcore/geospatial-support> <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/vcore/operators/aggregation

**B. The 100-document default limit.** Guidance still circulating — including current secondary search results and older mailing-list threads — tells readers to raise `$geoNear`'s default limit of 100 via a `limit` option. MongoDB removed both the option and the default in 4.2 (claim 17). Any advice mentioning `limit` or `num` inside `$geoNear` is pre-4.2 and should be read as stale; use a following `$limit` stage instead. The disagreement is one of source vintage, not of fact.

**Eight contradictions preserved side by side.** The consequential one is C1: mechanism.md says the `query` option is the documented selectivity lever and points at `GeoNearParams::baseBounds` in the source; practice.md has 2022 explain metrics showing `$geoNear` examining 177,470 documents where a `$match`-only plan examined 4,187 for the same 223 results; edge-cases.md calls the compound-index recommendation unverified folklore. I offered a reconciliation but did not assert it — whether a non-geo prefix actually generates index bounds can't be settled by reading.

11. A geospatial index cannot cover a query, so `$geoNear` always fetches documents; no index-only execution plan exists for it. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/restrictions/

12. A geospatial index cannot be used as a shard key, though a geospatial index can exist on a sharded collection keyed on a different field. This bounds how a sharded `$geoNear` can be routed: proximity is never the routing dimension. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/restrictions/

13. Index visibility under `readConcern: "majority"` is a real failure mode. `SERVER-20261` reports `$geoNear` on a `2d` index with `readConcern: majority` failing with `planner returned error: unable to find index for $geoNear query` on 3.1.7. It is Closed as a duplicate of `SERVER-20260` ("New indexes should bump their Collection's minimum SnapshotName"), i.e. the root cause is that a newly built index is not yet visible to the majority-committed snapshot. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-20261

24. Pre-4.2 `$geoNear` also inherited a hard 16 MB result ceiling from the underlying `geoNear` command, and exceeding it **silently discarded documents** while returning the partial result set with only a log warning. `SERVER-18965` is Closed/Done, affects 3.0.3, fix version **4.2**. This is the most severe historical failure mode: wrong answers with a success response. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-18965

32. On a time series collection, the `key` field is **required** and the `query` field is **forbidden**. Pre-filtering must move to a `$match` after the `$geoNear`, which means the filter cannot participate in index bound generation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations/

36. The 8.0 compatibility notes state the general rule directly: "Starting in MongoDB 8.0, you cannot use geospatial queries with malformed input. In prior versions, certain geospatial queries accept malformed input without an error." Note that this page does **not** enumerate the affected operators; the operator list comes from the `$geoNear` reference page, not from the release notes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/release-notes/8.0-compatibility/

41. `maxDistance` is therefore load-bearing for performance, not merely a filter: because `$geoNear` sorts nearest-first and (post-4.2) has no default limit, an unbounded `$geoNear` is a full ordered traversal of every indexed document. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/geonear-performance/247179 · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/rapid/release-notes/4.2-compatibility/

42. **Disconfirming evidence against the folk claim that 2dsphere proximity search is inherently slow.** `SERVER-13568` reported a `2dsphere` near query at 12,565 ms scanning 1,842,767 index entries where the equivalent `2d` query took under 1 ms scanning 1,000 entries, on 3M+ documents in 2.4.6. It was closed as a duplicate of `SERVER-19039` ("geoNear scans the same index cells multiple times, slowing down queries with many search intervals"), which is Closed/Done with fix version **3.1.6** (resolved 2015-07-20). The specific repeated-cell-scanning pathology is fixed; benchmarks and blog post

9. The `geoNear` *command* was deprecated in MongoDB 4.0: "Deprecated since version 4.0: Starting in version 4.0, MongoDB deprecates the `geoNear` command." Callers were directed to `$geoNear`, `$near`, or `$nearSphere`. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v4.0/source/reference/command/geoNear.txt

1. **Which version deprecated the `geoNear` command.** Alibaba Cloud's ApsaraDB compatibility page states "Starting from MongoDB 4.2, MongoDB deprecates the `geoNear` command." MongoDB's own 4.0 command reference says the command was *deprecated in 4.0*, and the 4.2 compatibility notes say it was *removed in 4.2*. The MongoDB sources are primary and mutually consistent; the Alibaba wording appears to collapse deprecation and removal into one release. Claims 9 and 10 follow the MongoDB sources. — https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/compatibility-changes-in-mongodb-4-2 — http

5. **The stage's behavior on sharded collections** (how results are merged across shards, and how ordering is preserved without a default limit) was not traced to a primary source in this pass and is not claimed here.

Explicitly **out of scope** (separate frontier items): the `$near` / `$nearSphere` query operators as standalone predicates, `$geoWithin` / `$geoIntersects`, the 2d and 2dsphere index types as concepts in their own right, GeoJSON as a format, and the removed legacy `geoNear` database command. Those appear here only where a `$geoNear` claim cannot be stated without them.

**A4. The `$facet` prohibition is independently documented**: `$facet` sub-pipelines cannot contain `$collStats`, `$facet`, `$geoNear`, `$indexStats`, `$out`, `$merge`, `$planCacheStats`, `$search`, `$searchMeta`, or `$vectorSearch`.

**D7. A `2d` index applies flat Euclidean geometry and does not handle wrap-around at the poles; MongoDB's own guidance is not to use a `2d` index for spherical queries over spherical data.** This is a correctness limit on `$geoNear`, not only a precision one.

**F3. A large search radius degrades `$geoNear` sharply.** This follows from C2 and C6: a wide band forces a large covering, a large buffered interval, and a large in-memory sort, and per A5 that buffer cannot spill. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/geonear-performance/247179 · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/exec/classic/near.h

21. `$geoNear` forces the query plan to start from the geospatial index. The `query` filter is evaluated against candidates produced by the outward distance walk; it does not narrow the search space first. Consequence: a selective non-geo filter makes `$geoNear` scan a much larger candidate set than the same filter would on its own. <https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/slow-performance-when-using-aggregation-along-with-geonear-with-multiple-query-condition/167850>

22. Measured instance of claim 21 (MongoDB 4.2.20, replica set on AWS, June 2022): identical result sets of 223 documents. This report covers only the MongoDB aggregation pipeline stage `$geoNear`: its introduction, its option surface over time, the behavioral breaks between major server releases, and where the authoritative record lives. The `geoNear` database command is covered only where it directly explains the stage's evolution (the stage absorbed it). Sibling operators (`$near`, `$nearSphere`, `$geoWithin`, `$geoIntersects`), geospatial index types (`2d`, `2dsphere`), and the wider MongoDB geospatial domain are out of scope.

This is a behavioural break for pipelines that passed a Polygon or LineString as `near`. <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear/> <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/operator/aggregation/geonear/>

26. On a sharded cluster the per-shard results of a proximity pipeline are merged by `mongos` unless an exception applies. Documented exceptions concern `$out`, `$lookup` against an unsharded collection, and sorting/grouping stages with `allowDiskUse` enabled — in the last case the merge runs on a randomly selected shard. `$geoNear` is not itself named among the stages that redirect the merge. <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-sharded-collections/>

**C. Whether `$geoNear` on a sharded collection has stage-specific merge behaviour.** The sharded aggregation page does not name `$geoNear` at all (claim 26), and the `$geoNear` reference page does not describe sharded merge semantics. Neither primary page confirms nor denies special handling. This gap was not closed by the sources consulted.

16. `$nearSphere` documents the same format-driven rule independently, which confirms it is a MongoDB-wide convention and not a `$geoNear` quirk: GeoJSON syntax takes `$minDistance`/`$maxDistance` in meters, legacy-pair syntax takes them in radians. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nearSphere/

20. A third-party report shows the confusion empirically: the same `geoNear` against the same data returned `1.49` (radians, ≈9,491 km) without spherical mode and `9501678.48` (meters) with `spherical: true`, and the reporter had to ask which unit applied. The issue was closed with no maintainer answer recorded and the repository was archived on 2020-11-11. — https://github.com/doctrine/mongodb/issues/173

31. On a time series collection, `$geoNear` is the **only** supported geospatial access path for sorting by proximity; `$near` and `$nearSphere` are not usable at all, and only `2dsphere` indexes are supported for this purpose. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations/

33. On a time series collection, `2d` indexes can only be created on the `metaField`, so legacy-coordinate `$geoNear` on a measurement field is not expressible. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations/

4. **Sharded-cluster split/merge behaviour for `$geoNear` is undocumented.** The aggregation-and-sharded-collections page does not mention `$geoNear` at all (https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-sharded-collections/), so it is not stated whether `$geoNear` forces a merge on `mongos`, how the nearest-first ordering is reconciled across shards, or how `allowDiskUse` affects merge placement for it. `SERVER-38716` records that sharded support was an explicit concern of the `$lookup` fix, implying non-trivial behaviour exists (https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-38716).

14. Migrating from the removed command to the stage is not mechanical. The command's `dis` output field becomes the stage's required `distanceField`; the command's boolean `includeLocs` becomes a string naming an output field; and the command's `avgDistance`/`maxDistance` summary statistics must be recomputed with a `$group` stage. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/docs/v4.2/source/release-notes/4.2-compatibility.txt — https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/compatibility-changes-in-mongodb-4-2

4. **Exact release that first allowed `$geoNear` inside a `$lookup` sub-pipeline.** The bound `let` example that makes this work is documented from 5.1 onward, and SERVER-54105 ("$geoNear in $lookup with dynamic ...") is the apparent tracking ticket, but the ticket body was not read and no release note was found that states the enablement version directly. Claim 15 asserts only what the 5.1 documentation states.

**A3. The stage's declared `StageConstraints` are:** `StreamType::kStreaming`, `PositionRequirement::kCustom`, `HostTypeRequirement::kTargetedShards`, `DiskUseRequirement::kNoDiskUse`, `FacetRequirement::kNotAllowed`, `TransactionRequirement::kAllowed`, `LookupRequirement::kAllowed`, `UnionRequirement::kAllowed`. These constants are the authoritative statement of where the stage may run: allowed inside transactions, inside a `$lookup` sub-pipeline, and inside `$unionWith`; never inside `$facet`; never spilling to disk.

**D1. `spherical` selects the distance model, and its meaning is conditional on the index.** With `spherical: true` the stage uses `$nearSphere` semantics and spherical geometry. With `spherical: false` (the default) it uses `$near` semantics — which is spherical on a `2dsphere` index and planar on a `2d` index. The flag therefore changes nothing on a `2dsphere` index in the GeoJSON case but changes everything on a `2d` index.

**D8. The underlying `2dsphere` index is always sparse and MongoDB ignores an explicit `sparse` option.** Documents missing the indexed field, or holding `null` or an empty array there, are absent from the index — and therefore invisible to `$geoNear`, which per B1 has no non-index path. Coordinates are bounded to longitude [-180, 180] and latitude [-90, 90].
**F2. On a sharded collection, a compound `2dsphere` index that includes the shard key, plus the shard key in `query`, narrows shard targeting.** Without it the stage fans out per C9.

**D4 — sharded-collection support history.** Current documentation describes sharded execution as supported with per-shard execution and a merge. I did not establish the version at which sharded `$geoNear` first worked, nor whether the MongoDB 4.2 removal of the legacy `geoNear` command is connected to that. Open.

**D6 — SBE.** All execution detail here is from the classic execution engine (`src/mongo/db/exec/classic/`). Whether a slot-based-execution path exists for `$geoNear`, and whether it preserves these invariants, was not investigated.

18. Migration mapping from the removed command: the command's `dis` output field becomes the stage's `distanceField` name, and the command's boolean `includeLocs` becomes a field name in the stage. <https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/compatibility-changes-in-mongodb-4-2>
